claims.text: The as-processed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy is initially a single-phase solid solution.
High-strain-rate loading causes the CoCrFeMnNi alloy to lose toughness.
High-strain-rate loading induces nanoscale phase segregation at grain boundaries.
The stress-induced grain-boundary segregation produces nanoscale ordered or intermetallic precipitates.
High-strain-rate loading produces localized adiabatic heating.
Stress concentrations develop at grain boundaries under high-strain-rate loading.
Localized adiabatic heating and grain-boundary stress concentrations trigger decomposition of the homogeneous solid solution.
The resulting grain-boundary precipitates are brittle.
Brittle grain-boundary precipitates act as preferential crack-nucleation sites.
Precipitate-assisted crack nucleation causes early intergranular fracture and reduced toughness.
At strain rates of at least 10^2 s^-1, samples will exhibit detectable grain-boundary nanoprecipitates.
At strain rates of at least 10^2 s^-1, samples will exhibit early crack initiation and intergranular brittle fracture.
Under quasi-static loading at approximately 10^-4 s^-1, the alloy will remain homogeneous and deform ductilely without observable nanoprecipitate formation.
The proposed controlled comparison uses identical samples tested at ambient temperature under approximately 10^-4 s^-1 and at least 10^2 s^-1 strain rates.
The proposed measurements combine microscopy, diffraction, fracture-surface analysis, and thermal imaging to relate grain-boundary changes and temperature spikes to fracture behavior.
The applicable service boundary is ambient-temperature dynamic loading represented by strain rates of at least 10^2 s^-1.
CoCrFeMnNi is inherently thermodynamically stable against the proposed decomposition.
